# 1 Samuel Chapter 13 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 126v-127r | **Source Image:** 1SA_013_page_001.jpg, 1SA_013_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Saul was [... ] years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two years over Israel.

**2** And Saul chose for himself three thousand men from Israel. And two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin. And the rest of the people he sent away, each man to his tent.

**3** And Jonathan struck the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. And Saul blew the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, "Let the Hebrews hear!"

**4** And all Israel heard it said that Saul had struck the garrison of the Philistines and also that Israel had become odious to the Philistines. And the people were called together after Saul to Gilgal.

**5** And the Philistines assembled to fight against Israel: thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen and people like the sand that is on the seashore in multitude. And they came up and encamped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven.

**6** And the men of Israel saw that they were in distress — for the people were hard-pressed — and the people hid themselves in caves and in thickets and among rocks and in tombs and in cisterns.

**7** And some of the Hebrews crossed the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. But Saul was still in Gilgal, and all the people trembled after him.

**8** And he waited seven days, according to the appointed time that Samuel had set. But Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the people were scattering from him.

**9** And Saul said, "Bring to me the burnt offering and the peace offerings." And he offered up the burnt offering.

**10** And it came to pass, as soon as he finished offering up the burnt offering, that behold, Samuel came! And Saul went out to meet him to greet him.

**11** And Samuel said, "What have you done?" And Saul said, "Because I saw that the people were scattering from me, and you did not come within the appointed days, and the Philistines were assembling at Michmash,

**12** and I said, 'Now the Philistines will come down against me to Gilgal, and I have not sought the favor of the LORD.' So I forced myself and offered up the burnt offering."

**13** And Samuel said to Saul, "You have acted foolishly. You have not kept the commandment of the LORD your God that he commanded you, for now the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.

**14** But now your kingdom shall not stand. The LORD has sought for himself a man after his own heart, and the LORD has appointed him as ruler over his people, because you have not kept that which the LORD commanded you."

**15** And Samuel arose and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul numbered the people who were found with him, about six hundred men.

**16** And Saul and Jonathan his son and the people who were found with them were dwelling in Geba of Benjamin, and the Philistines were encamped at Michmash.

**17** And the raiding party went out from the camp of the Philistines in three companies. One company turned toward the road to Ophrah, to the land of Shual.

**18** And one company turned toward the road to Beth-horon, and one company turned toward the road of the border that overlooks the Valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.

**19** Now no smith could be found in all the land of Israel, for the Philistines had said, "Lest the Hebrews make swords or spears."

**20** And all Israel would go down to the Philistines, each man to sharpen his plowshare and his mattock and his axe and his sickle.

**21** And the charge was a pim for the plowshares and for the mattocks, and a third of a shekel for sharpening the axes and for setting the goads.

**22** And it came to pass on the day of battle that neither sword nor spear was found in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan. But they were found with Saul and with Jonathan his son.

**23** And the garrison of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**Verse 1** — The MT reads: ben-shanah Sha'ul bemalko, lit. "Saul was a son of a year when he became king." The number has clearly fallen out of the text. The original age is irrecoverable from the MT. Some versions supply "thirty" or "forty" by conjecture; the LOGOS translation preserves the lacuna with brackets to reflect the manuscript evidence faithfully.

**Verse 3** — "Let the Hebrews hear!" ('ivrim): The term 'ivrim ("Hebrews") here may be the narrator's voice or may reflect Philistine terminology. Some scholars associate the term with the broader Habiru/Apiru designation.

**Verse 5** — "Thirty thousand chariots": The number is widely regarded as a textual corruption; some manuscripts and versions read "three thousand." The MT reading is preserved here as it stands in the Leningrad Codex.

**Verse 8** — This verse directly recalls Samuel's instruction in 10:8. Saul's failure to wait the full seven days constitutes disobedience to the prophetic command and inaugurates the rupture between prophetic authority and royal power.

**Verse 12** — Heb. wa'et'appaq: "I forced myself" (root 'apaq, "to restrain oneself"). Saul claims self-restraint before acting, but the verb ironically underscores his failure of restraint — he could not wait for Samuel.

**Verse 13-14** — Samuel's judgment is devastating: Saul's kingdom will not endure. The phrase 'ish kilbavo ("a man after his heart") points proleptically to David (cf. 16:7; Acts 13:22). The term nagid ("ruler") recurs, emphasizing that leadership is the LORD's appointment, not human presumption.

**Verse 19-22** — The Philistine iron monopoly reveals the depth of Israel's subjugation. The lack of smiths (charash) and the dependence on Philistine metalworkers for even agricultural tools illustrates both technological and military domination. Only Saul and Jonathan possess weapons — the kingship's fragility is starkly visible.

**Verse 21** — Heb. pim: A unit of weight (approximately 2/3 of a shekel, about 7.6 grams). Archaeological discoveries of inscribed pim weights have confirmed this otherwise obscure term.

-- LOGOS
